title: Uniform presentability ranks for an accessible ordinary functor
statement: Fix a universe $\mathcal U$; small sets and diagrams are relative to $\mathcal U$, all Hom sets are small, and colimits have the universal property of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. An infinite cardinal $\eta$ is regular if a union of fewer than $\eta$ sets each of cardinality less than $\eta$ has cardinality less than $\eta$. A category is $\eta$-filtered if every diagram with fewer than $\eta$ morphisms admits a cocone. An object $P$ is $\eta$-presentable if $\operatorname{Hom}(P,-)$ preserves small $\eta$-filtered colimits. A category is locally $\eta$-presentable if it has all small colimits and is generated under small $\eta$-filtered colimits by a small family of $\eta$-presentable objects; locally presentable means locally $\eta$-presentable for some infinite regular $\eta$. For infinite regular cardinals $\sigma<\tau$, write $\sigma\ll\tau$ when $a^b<\tau$ for every cardinal $a<\tau$ and $b<\sigma$. Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal D$ be locally presentable ordinary categories and let $H:\mathcal A\to\mathcal D$ preserve small $\alpha$-filtered colimits for an infinite regular $\alpha$. There is an infinite regular cardinal $\rho\geq\alpha$ such that, for every infinite regular $\tau$ with $\rho\ll\tau$, both $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal D$ are locally $\tau$-presentable, and $H$ takes $\tau$-presentable objects of $\mathcal A$ to $\tau$-presentable objects of $\mathcal D$. More generally, for any infinite regular $\sigma\geq\rho$, cardinals $\tau$ satisfying $\sigma\ll\tau$ exist above every prescribed small cardinal bound and have these same properties. The assertion concerns a sufficiently large choice of rank depending on $H$ and the categories; it does not assert preservation of $\alpha$-presentable objects.

source.place: HTT, Lemma 5.4.2.8, Proposition 5.4.2.9, Remark 5.4.2.11 and Remark 5.4.2.13 (printed pp. 425-427), in their ordinary-category specialization; Definition A.2.6.3 and the following observation (printed p. 819) for arbitrarily large sharp upper ranks. The proof of 5.4.2.13 bounds the ranks of the images of a small family of compact generators. Ordinary strong accessibility is also stated in Rosicky, Class-combinatorial model categories, Calais 2008 slides, printed p. 4 (https://www.math.muni.cz/~rosicky/papers/ct08a.pdf). Read online, not locally archived. No Stacks tag states this rank theorem.

proof.text: Choose infinite regular witness ranks $\kappa_A,\kappa_D$ for local presentability of $\mathcal A,\mathcal D$ and put $\kappa=\max(\alpha,\kappa_A,\kappa_D)$. This is one of these three regular cardinals. By [lem-coef-locally-presentable-rank-enlargement] both categories are locally $\kappa$-presentable. Choose a small family $(G_g)_{g\in S}$ of $\kappa$-presentable objects generating $\mathcal A$ under small $\kappa$-filtered colimits. Since $\kappa\geq\alpha$, every $\kappa$-filtered category is $\alpha$-filtered directly from the definition, so $H$ preserves these generating colimits.

Apply [lem-coef-object-presentability-rank] to each $H(G_g)$ in the locally presentable category $\mathcal D$, obtaining an infinite regular rank $\mu_g$ for that object. Apply [lem-coef-small-family-regular-bound] to the small family of sets consisting of the cardinals $\mu_g$ and one extra set of cardinality $\kappa$. It gives an infinite regular cardinal $\rho$ strictly above $\kappa$ and every $\mu_g$. In particular $\rho\geq\alpha$. The extra set supplies the bound even when $S$ is empty. All chosen ranks and their disjoint union are small in the fixed universe.

Fix any infinite regular $\tau$ with $\rho\ll\tau$. Thus $\tau>\rho>\kappa$ and $\kappa\ll\tau$, since an exponent $b<\kappa$ is also less than $\rho$. By [lem-coef-locally-presentable-rank-enlargement] both categories are locally $\tau$-presentable. Each $H(G_g)$ is $\tau$-presentable: every $\tau$-filtered category is $\mu_g$-filtered, so its Hom functor preserves these colimits by the definition of $\mu_g$-presentability. This monotonicity needs no separate lemma.

Let $P$ be any $\tau$-presentable object of $\mathcal A$. Choose a small $\kappa$-filtered presentation $F_0:I\to\mathcal A$ of $P$ with values among the $G_g$. Apply [lem-coef-cardinal-filtered-poset-reindex] to $I$ with $\eta=\kappa$: it gives a small $\kappa$-filtered partially ordered set $\Pi$ and $u:\Pi\to I$ such that the restricted cocone exhibits $P$ as a colimit of $F=F_0\circ u:\Pi\to\mathcal A$, whose values are still among the $G_g$. By step 3, $\kappa<\tau$ are infinite regular and $\mu^\nu<\tau$ for $\mu<\tau$, $\nu<\kappa$. Apply [lem-coef-sharp-filtered-poset-subsets] with $\alpha=\kappa$, $\beta=\tau$ and $A=\Pi$. Its poset $B$ consists of subsets $J\subseteq\Pi$ with $|J|<\tau$ in which every subset of fewer than $\kappa$ elements has an upper bound in $J$; it is small, covers $\Pi$, and every family of fewer than $\tau$ members, including the empty one, has an upper bound in $B$. Regard each $J$ as a full subposet. It is a $\kappa$-filtered category: a diagram with fewer than $\kappa$ morphisms has fewer than $\kappa$ objects, and an upper bound in $J$ of these objects is a cocone, all diagrams commuting in a poset. It has fewer than $\tau$ morphisms, since they are among the pairs in $J\times J$, a finite set or of cardinality $|J|<\tau$. In the same way $B$ is a nonempty $\tau$-filtered poset. Every arrow $p\leq q$ of $\Pi$ lies in some member: take an upper bound of members containing $p$ and $q$; being a full subposet, it contains the arrow.

source.place: HTT Lemma 5.4.2.8 and proof of Proposition 5.4.2.9 (printed pp. 425-426): reindexing by a kappa-filtered poset and its tau-small kappa-filtered subsets

proof.text: For $J\in B$ choose $Q_J=\operatorname{colim}_{J}F|_J$ with its cocone. Inclusions $J\subseteq K$ induce the unique maps $Q_J\to Q_K$ compatible with these cocones; uniqueness proves identities and composition. The resulting cocone $Q\to P$ is colimiting: a compatible family $Q_J\to X$ gives a map $F(p)\to X$ by choosing a member containing $p$; a common upper bound for two members makes this independent of choice, and a member containing any given arrow proves naturality. Conversely every cocone $F\to X$ on $F:\Pi\to\mathcal A$ restricts to each $J$ and induces a unique compatible family. These two operations are inverse, so the universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] identifies $P$ with $\operatorname{colim}_{J\in B}Q_J$.

By $\tau$-presentability of $P$, the canonical map $\operatorname{colim}_{J\in B}\operatorname{Hom}(P,Q_J)\to\operatorname{Hom}(P,P)$ is a bijection. Since $B$ is small and filtered, clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise] supplies a representative $s:P\to Q_J$ of the inverse image of $1_P$. If $r:Q_J\to P$ is the colimit-cocone component, the formula for the canonical map gives $rs=1_P$. Thus $P$ is a retract of this particular $Q_J$.

source.place: HTT proof of Proposition 5.4.2.9; compactness/retract argument written explicitly

proof.text: The category $J$ is $\kappa$-filtered (step 4) and $\kappa\geq\alpha$, so $H$ preserves the defining colimit of $Q_J$ by step 1. Therefore $H(Q_J)$ is a colimit of $H\circ F|_J$, indexed by a small category with fewer than $\tau$ morphisms. All its values are among the $H(G_g)$, hence $\tau$-presentable by step 3. Apply [lem-coef-ordinary-small-colimit-presentable] in $\mathcal D$ to conclude that $H(Q_J)$ is $\tau$-presentable. This application uses the smallness of $J$, not any claim that the entire poset $B$ has fewer than $\tau$ members.

source.place: HTT Remark 5.4.2.13 and the small-colimit calculation underlying Proposition 5.4.2.9

proof.text: Applying $H$ to $rs=1_P$ exhibits $A=H(P)$ as a retract of $Q=H(Q_J)$, with maps $u=H(s):A\to Q$ and $v=H(r):Q\to A$ satisfying $vu=1_A$. For each $T\in\mathcal D$, put $i_T(f)=f\circ v$ and $r_T(g)=g\circ u$, from $\operatorname{Hom}(A,T)$ to $\operatorname{Hom}(Q,T)$ and back. Then $r_Ti_T(f)=fvu=f$, and postcomposition with any $T\to T\prime$ commutes with both maps by associativity. For a small $\tau$-filtered diagram $T:L\to\mathcal D$ with colimit $Z$, these maps induce maps $i_X,r_X$ on the two colimits of Hom sets by [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]; their composite is the identity because it is the identity on every cocone component. Put $i_Y=i_Z$ and $r_Y=r_Z$. If $a:X\to Y$ and $b:U\to V$ are respectively the Hom comparison maps for $A$ and $Q$, their formulas $[\ell,f]\mapsto c_\ell f$ give $bi_X=i_Ya$ and $ar_X=r_Yb$. The map $b$ is bijective by step 7. Hence $r_Xb^{-1}i_Y$ is inverse to $a$: its composite on the right with $a$ is $r_Xb^{-1}bi_X=1_X$, and its composite on the left with $a$ is $r_Ybb^{-1}i_Y=1_Y$. Thus $\operatorname{Hom}(A,-)$ preserves every such colimit, so $H(P)$ is $\tau$-presentable.

Finally fix any infinite regular $\sigma\geq\rho$ and any prescribed small cardinal bound $b$. Choose an infinite small cardinal $\lambda\geq\max(\sigma,b)$, put $c=2^\lambda$ and $\tau=c^+$. By [lem-coef-infinite-cardinal-successor-regular] this $\tau$ is infinite regular, and $\tau>\lambda\geq b,\sigma$. For $a<\tau$ and $d<\sigma$ we have $a\leq c$ and $d\leq\lambda$, so $a^d\leq(2^\lambda)^d=2^{\lambda\cdot d}\leq2^\lambda=c<\tau$ (including $d=0$). Hence $\sigma\ll\tau$. Every $\tau$ with $\sigma\ll\tau$ also satisfies $\rho\ll\tau$, by restricting the exponents to $d<\rho$; steps 3-8 therefore give the same conclusions for all these $\tau$. This proves both existence above every bound and the full quantified final clause.

lean.statement: theorem accessible_functor_presentability_ranks {A : Type u₁} {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v} A] [Category.{v} D] [IsLocallyPresentable.{v} A] [IsLocallyPresentable.{v} D] (alpha : Cardinal.{v}) [Fact alpha.IsRegular] (H : A ⥤ D) [H.IsCardinalAccessible alpha] : ∃ (rho : Cardinal.{v}) (_ : Fact rho.IsRegular), alpha ≤ rho ∧ (∀ (tau : Cardinal.{v}) [Fact tau.IsRegular], (rho < tau ∧ (∀ (a b : Cardinal.{v}), a < tau → b < rho → a ^ b < tau)) → IsCardinalLocallyPresentable A tau ∧ IsCardinalLocallyPresentable D tau ∧ ∀ (P : A), IsCardinalPresentable P tau → IsCardinalPresentable (H.obj P) tau) ∧ (∀ (sigma : Cardinal.{v}) [Fact sigma.IsRegular], rho ≤ sigma → ∀ (bound : Cardinal.{v}), ∃ (tau : Cardinal.{v}) (hTau : Fact tau.IsRegular), bound < tau ∧ sigma < tau ∧ (∀ (a b : Cardinal.{v}), a < tau → b < sigma → a ^ b < tau) ∧ @IsCardinalLocallyPresentable A inferInstance tau hTau ∧ @IsCardinalLocallyPresentable D inferInstance tau hTau ∧ ∀ (P : A), @IsCardinalPresentable A inferInstance P tau hTau → @IsCardinalPresentable D inferInstance (H.obj P) tau hTau)
